text.p: Jordan-Kuwait Bank management on Tuesday won approval from a majority of shareholders to double its capital to 20 million dinars ($28 million) after overcoming opposition from dissenting investors.
The bank succeeded in getting approval of 56 percent of its shareholders during an extraordinary general assembly held to approve the capital increase.
The meeting had been rescheduled from last week after it failed to get a 50 percent quorum when dissenting shareholders withdrew at the last minute.
A new seven-member board of directors was elected with three seats held by a consortium of Kuwaiti investors led by Kuwait Investment Projects Company.
The bank has resisted merger attempts by Bank of Jordan's chairman, Tawfiq Fakhouri, who owns around 28 percent.
It was helped by bloc sales by Kuwaiti shareholders last month estimated at around 7.5 million dinars which raised their stake to 45 percent of the bank's capital from around 30 percent.

The Central Bank has been trying to strengthen Jordan's banking system by encouraging mergers between smaller banks and setting all banks a minimum capital level of 20 million dinars by the end of 1997.
Jordan-Kuwait Bank plans to double its capital by transferring 4.5 million dinars from reserves and retained profits and raise another 5.5 million dinars through share subscription.
